exclusions.text: Step 0 — Is your system explicitly excluded from the AI Act's scope?
exclusions.help: Before checking risk, determine if the Act applies to this activity at all.

options.label: Used exclusively for military, defense, or national security purposes.
Developed and put into service solely for scientific research and development (not for market use).
Used by a natural person for purely personal, non-professional activity.
Research/development of AI models prior to placing them on the market (unless tested in "real-world conditions").
Used by a non-EU public authority under international law-enforcement cooperation agreements.

outcome.note: One or more scope exclusions apply — no AI Act obligations apply to this system.

annex-i.text: Step 1 — Annex I "Product Safety" filter: does the system serve as a safety component (or is it the product itself) for any of these?
annex-i.help: The AI Act automatically classifies AI as High-Risk if integrated into products already subject to EU health and safety laws.

options.label: Medical Devices (e.g. diagnostic software, robotic surgery).
Toys or Personal Transport (e.g. smart toys, e-scooters).
Machinery & Industrial Tools (e.g. collaborative robots).
Lifts, Pressure Equipment, or Gaseous Fuel Appliances.
Marine, Aviation, or Rail Equipment.
Motor Vehicles (e.g. ADAS or autonomous driving features).

annex-iii.text: Step 2 — Annex III "Sensitive Use Case" filter: does the system fall into any of these high-impact domains?
annex-iii.help: Even if your product isn't a "machine", it is High-Risk if used in these domains.

options.label: Remote Biometric Identification — identifying people at a distance in public/private spaces.
Biometric Categorization — sorting people based on sensitive traits (gender, race, etc.).
Emotion Recognition — detecting emotional states in workplaces or schools.
Critical Infrastructure — safety components managing/operating road traffic, or water/gas/heating/electricity supply.
Critical Infrastructure — cybersecurity protecting the digital integrity of essential utility networks.
Education — systems determining access or admission to schools/universities.
Education — grading exams or evaluating learning outcomes that steer a person's career path.
Education — detecting "cheating" or prohibited behavior during assessments.
Employment & HR — sorting CVs, ranking candidates, or placing targeted job ads.
Employment & HR — decisions on promotions, terminations, or task allocation based on behavior.
Essential Services — determining eligibility for social security, housing, or healthcare.
Essential Services — assessing creditworthiness, loan approval, or insurance pricing (life/health).
Essential Services — systems used for 112/999 calls or dispatching first responders.
Law Enforcement — predicting the risk of a person becoming a victim or re-offending.
Law Enforcement — evaluating the reliability of evidence or polygraphs.
Law Enforcement — automated processing of personal data to evaluate criminal risk.
Migration/Border — checking travel documents or detecting fraudulent identities.
Migration/Border — evaluating visa or asylum applications and security risks.
Migration/Border — monitoring, detecting, and identifying people at borders.
Justice/Democracy — used by a judicial authority to research facts or interpret the law.
Justice/Democracy — systems used to influence the outcome of an election or voters' behavior.

practical-rights.text: Step 3 — The Practical Rights Test: even if not listed in Annex III, does the system do any of the following?
practical-rights.help: Practical rule: if the AI affects someone's rights, opportunities, or economic wellbeing, treat as High-Risk.

options.label: Influences access to employment — significantly impacts who gets seen or hired.
Influences access to finance — determines who gets loans, credit, or insurance.
Influences access to healthcare — prioritizes or denies medical treatment/insurance.
Influences access to education — affects admission or career-defining grades.
Influences access to essential public services — determines social security or housing.
Contributes to legal or administrative decisions — directly informs a judge or official's ruling on a citizen.

outcome.note: Source checklist only distinguishes high-risk vs. not-high-risk — it does not determine prohibited status or the limited/minimal split. See docs/context/decision-trees/high-risk-classification.md.

escape-hatch.text: Step 4 — Article 6(3) "Escape Hatch": does the system meet any of these ancillary-task criteria?
escape-hatch.help: You cannot use this exemption if the system performs Profiling (automated assessment of personal traits/behavior) — profiling ticked earlier makes it High-Risk regardless of this step.

options.label: Narrow Procedural Task — a tiny, administrative sub-step (e.g. formatting text).
Improving Human Activity — only improves the result of a previous human decision.
Preparatory Task — only organizes data or flags patterns for a later human assessment.
Pattern Detection — identifies deviations but does not influence the final decision.

outcome.note: The Art. 6(3) exemption cannot apply because a profiling-type trigger (Step 2) was ticked — profiling is High-Risk regardless of this step.
Exempt under the Art. 6(3) ancillary-task escape hatch.
